options.text: $f(x)$ does not attain value within the interval [-2,2]
$f(x)$ takes on the value $2 \frac{1}{3}$ in the interval [-2,2]
$f(x)$ takes on the value $3 \frac{1}{4}$ in the interval [-2,2]
$f(x)$ takes no value $\rho, 1    < p < 5$ in the interval [-2,2]

solution.text:
\(f(-2)=1\) and \(f(2)=5\) and \(f\) is continuous also.
So intermediate value theorem, function \(f(x)\) takes all values between 1 to 5 .
\(\Rightarrow \quad 2 \frac{1}{3}\) and \(3 \frac{1}{4}\) lies in 1 to 5 so option \(B, C\) are correct
